source_review.notes: Checked current Java SE 26 Chapter 17, official Go memory model, current Rust undefined-behavior reference, Herlihy-Wing linearizability, Boehm-Adve DRF foundations, FastTrack, AVIO, Lu et al. concurrency-bug study, Herlihy et al. second edition, and the scalable-commutativity paper. Language-specific consequences remain attributed to their specifications rather than generalized.

evidence: Checked conflict, invariant, precondition, transition, implementation-event, invocation, response, real-time order, and linearization notation.
Checked separation of location-level data-race conditions from operation-level history conditions.
Checked serializability and strict-serializability terminology is qualified by platform definitions.
notation_and_syntax.notes: The chapter does not assert one universal racy-program semantics across languages.

evidence: Recomputed 4!/(2!2!)=6 check/reserve schedules.
Enumerated four schedules in which both checks precede the decisive competing reservation and oversubscribe.
Confirmed two serialized schedules preserve one-slot capacity and maximum accepted count is two in the flawed model.
numerical_recomputation.notes: Counts apply only to the four-event sequentially consistent model.

evidence: Re-derived reserve-if-positive as one conditional abstract transition preserving accepted <= capacity.
Checked conditional version commit turns stale replacement into explicit no-state-change conflict.
Checked linearization requirements: point within invocation/response, legal sequential history, and real-time precedence.
symbolic_recomputation.notes: Operation histories and memory events are separate reasoning levels.

evidence: Reviewed check-then-act, read-modify-write, lost update, duplicate creation, winner selection, TOCTOU, stale authorization, and async suspension races.
Reviewed rollback, retry, crash, duplicate effect, process boundaries, multiple locks, stale versions, and external side effects before commit.
Reviewed dynamic detector gaps, custom synchronization, unexecuted paths, foreign code, and logical races over atomics.
Reviewed medication and hospital scheduling cases for clinical, safety, privacy, finance, operations, and regulatory authority.
boundary_and_adversarial_cases.notes: High-consequence examples require current named human review; none is claimed.

evidence: Traced product invariant to atomic region and serialization authority in every repair pattern.
Confirmed stale observations are validated or made irrelevant at authoritative commit.
Confirmed abortable regions do not emit irreversible effects without durable reservation/outbox design.
Confirmed retry recomputes premises and proposed linearization points survive failure/rollback.
invariant_checking.notes: A mechanism is accepted only when its scope covers all writers and state in the invariant.

evidence: Reviewed the minimal quota counterexample and conditional-transition repair.
Reviewed why atomic component methods do not imply atomic composition.
Reviewed history mapping for linearizability and real-time order.
Reviewed counterexamples involving uniqueness after pre-commit effects and individually linearizable objects with a cross-object invariant.
proof_review.notes: The chapter gives bounded proof obligations and counterexamples, not a universal detector or repair theorem.

evidence: Audited uses of atomic, race-free, linearizable, serializable, safe, unique, exactly once, authority, and prove.
Confirmed source expressions and thread-safe methods are never presumed compound-atomic.
Confirmed detector silence and passing schedule tests are not presented as absence proof.
proof_sketch_labeling.notes: All correctness terms retain explicit abstraction, language, and history scope.

evidence: artifacts/snippets/CONPAR-005/report.json records deterministic execution for check-then-reserve-race.
The chapter limits the artifact to six synthetic schedules and no real memory model.
Race detectors, atomicity detectors, systematic schedules, history checkers, assertions, and static analysis are labeled as different evidence.
empirical_evidence_labeling.notes: No production race freedom, financial integrity, filesystem safety, clinical safety, regulatory approval, or external review is claimed.

conceptual_review.notes: Reviewed race condition, data race, conflict, atomic action, atomicity violation, check-then-act, RMW, TOCTOU, lost update, winner race, invariant, serialization authority, conditional commit, linearization point, linearizability, serializability, and strict serializability as distinct concepts.

practitioner_review.notes: Reviewed minimal schedule construction, lock scope, conditional RMW, database versions/constraints, transactions, ownership, outbox, idempotency, stable handles, deterministic hooks, race detection, history checking, replay, failure, retry, and compatibility. Internal concurrency-practitioner-oriented review only.

pedagogical_review.notes: Verified progression from terminology through invariant discovery, counterexample traces, serialization authority, repair choices, linearizability, evidence, failures, and high-consequence transfer. Ten examples and five complete exercises cover definition, tracing, protocol repair, trade-off comparison, and unfamiliar design.

limitations: Internal evidence record only; no external academic, language-memory-model, concurrency, database, filesystem, API, security, finance, clinical, hospital-operations, privacy, safety, quality, regulatory, or practitioner review is claimed.
